modelDefinition.name: PlexSpecification
modelDefinition.description: Vendor-shaped projection of SpecificationDto from /quality/v1/part-specifications. Generated from the PLEX dictionary 2026-08-05, not hand-written. Read-only evidence: every field is nullable because a vendor's required flag describes their write contract, not what their read endpoint returns. Harmonization happens in the hub tenant.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Primary id (== dedupeKey). Ours, not the vendor's.

fields.name: partId
fields.description: The Part ID.

fields.name: partNumber
fields.description: Specify the part number requiring specifications.

fields.name: partRevision
fields.description: Specify the part revision requiring specifications.

fields.name: specificationNumber
fields.description: The Specification Number of the Part Specification.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The description of the Part Specification.

fields.name: formula
fields.description: The specification formula. Formulas are used when a spec is calculated based on one or more other specs. For example, if a rectangular part includes specs for length and height, a calculated spec can be implemented to determine square inches: [60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34] * [7acbf6bb-727b-4714-bf18-8c3f82a45f8c] Dependent specifications are contained within brackets and referenced by ID. When entering functions into the formula, make sure you use the proper character for separating the parameters. Mathematical Expressions Functions AVG MAX MIN SUM STDEV SIN COS TAN ARCSIN ACOS ARCCOS ATAN ARCTAN LN LOG SQRT ABS Constants PI C E Operators *, +, -, /, ^ % DIV MOD Here is an example formula using a combination of supported functions, constants and operators defined above: Pi * min([60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34], [7acbf6bb-727b-4714-bf18-8c3f82a45f8c]) Parameters to defined functions are separated by a comma, but this delimiter may also be overridden by the Plex setting List Delimiter (Lists Setting Group). Aggregate Functions Aggregate functions can be used in the formula to provide functionality across a set of measurements for a single specification. This is achieved by the use of any aggregate function (min, max, avg, sum) in conjunction with a "token parameter" to indicate which specification(s) are being used as aggregates. The Formula Type assigned to the formula is used to specify One-To-One (the setting by which all existing formula work) or Many-To-One (used when aggregating a measurement set down to a single value). For example, if specification A includes 3 measurements, a calculated specification B can utilize an aggregate formula to calculate a single value: | Specification | Measurements | ID | Formula | Formula Type | | ----| ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | A | 10, 20, 30 | 60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34 | | | B | 20 | 7acbf6bb-727b-4714-bf18-8c3f82a45f8c | avg([60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34:aggregate=true) | Many-To-One | A formula type of One-To-One is the existing behavior of a formula, but it can be used in conjunction with aggregate functions to allow a single sample measurement to be used to output multiple measurements: | Specification | Measurements | ID | Formula | Formula Type | | ----| ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | C | 10, 0, -10 | 7acbf6bb-727b-4714-bf18-8c3f82a45f8c | sum([7acbf6bb-727b-4714-bf18-8c3f82a45f8c:aggregate=true) - [60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34] | One-To-One | Historical Data Special token parameters can be used to pull measurement data from past checksheets. A number of past checksheets to be used must be supplised along with an aggregate function (if applicable). The number of past checksheets that can be used in a calculation is limited to 50. For example, this formula is used to calculate the average value of a given specification for the last 5 submitted checksheets: avg([60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34:pastchecksheets=5 pastfunction=avg]) If an aggregate is not necessary, the pastfunction argument can be set to none: avg([60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34:pastchecksheets=5 pastfunction=none]) Note: it is important to use the "none" aggregation option in formulas where f(x0,...,xn) does not equal f(f(x0,...,xn-1), xn). For example, min(4, 6, 5) is equivalent to min(min(4,6), 5), while stdev(4, 6, 5) is not equivalent to stdev(stdev(4,6), 5). Offsheet Historical Data Historical data can also be referenced by using offsheet token parameters. This is used to pull aggregated measurements from data entered on any prior checksheet. The number of past checksheets must be specified as a separate checksheet specification measurement. This number is then referenced in subsequent formulas. For example, to pull the average value of a specification from a specific number of other checksheets, where its specification ID is 7acbf6bb-727b-4714-bf18-8c3f82a45f8c, a new specification should be created referencing this ID (We'll call the specification Sample Size): [7acbf6bb-727b-4714-bf18-8c3f82a45f8c:offsheetcalc=samplesize] Assuming the ID of the above specification is 60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34, we can then create a second specification called 'Average' with the following formula: [60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34:offsheetcalc=avg] The above specification value will be calculated using the past X number of prior checksheets, where X is equal to the Sample Size specification value. Restrictions The number of checksheets for the sample size is limited to a maximum of 50. The measurements are Container Serial specific. This means that if a container is not specified then all checksheet measurements will be used. As Serialized Checksheets are Container specific (per row), the container serial must be set. Attributes Attributes of a specification can be used as part of the formula. The supported attributes are tolerance, target, min, and max. Attribute usage in a formula will appear as follows: [60bdc4fa-67ea-4d25-b95c-06f67225db34:attribute=tolerance]

fields.name: formulaType
fields.description: The specification formula type.

fields.name: defaultGageType
fields.description: The gage type defaulted on a control plan when specification is added.

fields.name: plcName
fields.description: The name of an associated programmable logic controller(PLC).

fields.name: specialSymbol
fields.description: The special symbol to use for the part specification.

fields.name: customerSpecified
fields.description: Specifies that this is a part specification that your customer expects to be verified or not.

fields.name: note
fields.description: A short description or name for the specification. This typically comes from the drawing.

fields.name: functionRequirementType
fields.description: The function requirement type of the part specification.

fields.name: specificationDimensionType
fields.description: The specification dimension type of the part specification.

fields.name: updatedDateTime
fields.description: The latest date this specification was updated.

fields.name: externalId
fields.description: Native key in the source system. Half of the upsert key, so a re-extract overwrites rather than duplicates.

fields.name: sourceSystemId
fields.description: FK to ExternalSystem — WHICH instance of this ERP said so. Two sites running the same vendor are two systems, and their keys collide by construction.

fields.name: sourceUrl
fields.description: Collection endpoint this row was read from, so a suspect field can be traced to the contract that produced it.

fields.name: sourceVersion
fields.description: Dictionary stamp this model was generated from. A vendor schema change shows up here before it shows up as a bug.

fields.name: syncedAt
fields.description: When this row was last read from the source.

fields.name: rawPayload
fields.description: The verbatim vendor record. Stays in the SPOKE tenant — feature bundles cross to the hub, raw payloads never do.

fields.name: dedupeKey
fields.description: sourceSystemId:externalId — the idempotency key.

fields.name: partRefId
fields.description: Resolved reference to PlexPart, computed by the data mapping as sourceSystemId + ":" + partId. Nullable: a row may load before its target, and a null FK is not validated.
